key_insight: Scientific machine learning can replace expensive full-order simulations for coupled fluid flow and transport by combining physics constraints with reduced-order and neural surrogate models.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates can accelerate prediction for multiscale flow problems such as turbidity currents and thermal convection, enabling faster design studies and more computationally efficient HPC workflows.
method: SVD-based reduced-order models, including Dynamic Mode Decomposition
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for governing-equation-aware surrogates
β-Variational Autoencoders (β-VAEs) to extract disentangled nonlinear modes
evidence_signal: The chapter supports its methods with representative benchmarks and case studies, including lock-exchange flows, turbidity currents, and Rayleigh-Bénard convection.
watch_item: Performance and generalization depend strongly on the specific data regime, coupling strength, and modeling assumptions, so real-time use and uncertainty quantification are not guaranteed.
paper_title: Advances in Scientific Machine Learning for Coupled Fluid Flow and Transport
